descriptionChirho: An elevated platform or chair from which a magistrate or ruler pronounces judgment, used for both Roman civil courts and the eschatological divine tribunal. Multilingual evidence is strikingly consistent: Spanish 'tribunal,' Hindi 'न्याय-आसन' (judgment-seat), Arabic 'كُرسيّ القضاء' (chair of judgment) and 'مِنبر' (pulpit/platform), Korean '재판석' (court seat), Swahili 'kiti cha hukumu' (chair of judgment) and 'kiti cha enzi' (throne of authority). This is the dominant sense (11 of 12 occurrences), appearing in contexts like Pilate's judgment seat (Matt 27:19, John 19:13), Gallio's tribunal (Acts 18:12), and the eschatological judgment seat of Christ (Rom 14:10, 2 Cor 5:10).

A single pace or footstep, denoting a minimal measure of land area. This rare literal sense appears once (Acts 7:5) where God gave Abraham not even a foot's breadth of the promised land. The translations diverge sharply from the tribunal sense: Spanish 'paso' (pace/step), Hindi 'पैर रखने की जगह' (place to put a foot), Arabic 'مَوطِئ' (footprint/tread), Korean '발 의' (of a foot), Swahili 'hatua' (step/stride). Every language uses a locomotion or spatial term rather than a judicial one, confirming this is a genuinely distinct sense rooted in the physical meaning of the Greek word — a raised surface one steps on.
